cheng: Hey — ran a long-run repro on the interleaved-prefix case. Under sustained multi-tenant chat load with ~150 concurrent sessions we start seeing a pattern: short-lived prefixes are evicting hot prefixes mid-conversation, causing 2x token-generation stalls for affected requests.

maria: ugh. is this the same fragmentation we saw last quarter or new behavior?

cheng: Related but different. Last time it was cold-start churn on node restart. This one happens on steady-state: small prefixes from bursty sessions interleave and bump larger-session prefixes out of residency. Eviction traces show alternating eviction/insert churn for the same LRU buckets.

ash: can you paste the cache key format you're using? curious if key granularity is amplifying duplicates.

cheng: Key format is currently: model:v2|tenant_id|session_id_prefix_hash|prefix_len_bucket|seq_start. Example: 
``` 
redwood/gptq-v2|tenant-42|sph:0x7a9f|len:32|s:0
```
We bucket prefix_len coarsely which compresses different prefixes into similar residency bins — might be making LRU decisions noisy.

mike: that bucketed len was to limit unique key explosion right? but it does reduce hit specificity.

lina: also the runtime switches kernels once total context > 1024, so some requests extend KV lifetimes and hold pages longer. kernel switch + eviction churn could explain the 2x stall windows.

cheng: Exactly. Profiling timeline: when a large-session request enters kernel-B path, it pins ~1.6x more KV pages during generation. Meanwhile many small bursts insert short prefixes in same shard causing migration. I attached a snippet of the eviction log pattern: 
``` 
[evict] shard=13 key=... len=32 resident=1 time=162345.23
[insert] shard=13 key=... len=8 resident=0 time=162345.24
[evict] shard=13 key=... len=96 resident=1 time=162345.25
```
Churn happens within milliseconds.

maria: what are our metrics showing? eviction rate, prefix_reuse_ratio, mem_pressure?

cheng: quick numbers from the run (60m):
- kv_eviction_rate: 4.8k evictions/min (baseline was 1.1k)
- prefix_reuse_ratio: dropped from 0.62 -> 0.38 for sessions >1k tokens
- median_fill_latency (on miss): 8.2ms -> 18.6ms
- tail-99 latency for token gen increased 2.1x for affected tenants

lina: big hit. any evidence of hash collisions between session_id_prefix_hash?

cheng: low collision rate. Hotness comes from shard-level locality & len-bucketing. Two proposals: 1) remove prefix_len_bucket (fine-grained len in key) and cap per-tenant prefix count; 2) add sticky residency hint for session-affine prefixes (session-scoped LRU that resists eviction for short window).

mike: tradeoffs: finer keys -> higher memory for keys and potentially more unique entries, sticky hints -> better per-session UX but can hoard KV space. What about prefetch eviction fences? e.g., track top-N prefixes per session and grant them a soft residency weight.

maria: also consider switching eviction policy to a segmented-LRU (S-LRU) where a protected segment holds session-affine prefixes for a tunable window. That reduces both fragmentation and starvation.

ops-bot: Experiment created: evict-protect-2026-03-15 (variant: s-lru + no-len-bucket). ID=exp-7281. Duration=2h.

cheng: ran a canary with s-lru (protected segment size = 8 prefixes/session) + remove len bucket. Results (30m steady state):
- kv_eviction_rate: 1.4k evictions/min
- prefix_reuse_ratio: 0.59
- median_fill_latency: 9.1ms
- tail-99 token latency improvement: ~18% better than baseline
Memory increase: +5.8% total KV resident memory (due to more distinct keys)

lina: 5.8% seems acceptable given tail improvements. Did you see any regression in throughput or batching behavior?

cheng: Throughput unchanged at p95. But we noticed slightly larger batch variance: protected prefixes stay resident and sometimes create heavier KV read bursts when a protected session resumes, increasing instantaneous GPU kernel load. Batching heuristics handled it but we should adjust max-batch-size ceiling down by 10% for protected-shard nodes.

mike: can we avoid removing len-bucket initially? maybe add per-shard residency counters and use them to deprioritize short-lived prefixes dynamically. That keeps key space smaller but still avoids evicting hot long-session prefixes.

maria: good idea. Also instrument a new metric: prefix_residency_half_life per session to detect sessions that should get sticky protection.

cheng: action items:
- (cheng) push PR for S-LRU + residency counters prototype (will keep len-bucket for first pass): small memory delta expected.
- (ash) add metric prefix_residency_half_life and kv_shard_eviction_skew to console.
- (mike) run perf test with kernel-A/B mix (simulate >1024 context) to validate batching ceiling tweak.
- (lina) write short experiment plan to test 'protected segment size' parameter sweep (2,4,8,16).

ash: also put a quick doc note on cache-key hygiene: avoid mixing sequence_start in key when session affinity would be better represented with session_prefix_id. That reduces pseudo-unique keys from small seq shifts.

cheng: agreed. I'll update key schema proposal to: model|tenant|session_prefix_id|prefix_fingerprint (fingerprint = sha1(prefix) truncated) and drop seq_start from top-level key.

maria: sounds good. please reference perf numbers in the PR.

mike: thanks — if s-lru looks stable in canaries, we should roll to staging and watch kv_eviction_rate and prefix_reuse_ratio for 24h.

lina: +1. Also add a short note about kernel transitions in the rollout doc; operators should know the extra memory/kernels interplay.

cheng: will do. I'll post the PR and experiment logs here when ready. tl;dr: fragmentation + len-bucket + kernel path switch caused interleaved eviction race; S-LRU + hygiene fixes looks promising with small memory cost. :mechanical_arm:
